I'll investigate the current split between Rust and JVM code before weighing in.

                                <property name="pathland.native.staging" value="${project.basedir}/target/native" />
                                <available file="${pathland.native.staging}" type="dir" property="pathland.native.staged" />
                                <property name="pathland.native.host" value="${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html${pathland.native.ext}" />

                                    <condition>
                                        <and>
                                            <not><isset property="pathland.native.staged" /></not>
                                            <not><isset property="pathland.native.host.present" /></not>
                                        </and>
                                    </condition>

# pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 28, 2026

The **Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a
thin **JNA shim** over `libpathland_render_html`. There is a **single renderer**
(the Rust crate), reused by every language; the former hand-written retained
Java renderer is removed. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Stateless JNA shim**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` links the Rust cdylib;
  `render(frame, root)` / `renderFragment(frame, root)` /
  `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a self-contained snapshot frame to
  HTML in one pass (no retained tree, no `applyFrame`); `pathland_html_free`
  releases native strings. Lazy-loaded; skipped (test assumption) when the dylib
  is absent from `java.library.path`.
- **Debug comments**: `renderDebug(frame, root)` / `renderFragmentDebug(...)`
  bind the Rust `pathland_html_render_debug` exports — each rendered node is
  prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers
  applied (opt-in; the plain `render` output is unchanged).
- **Full Rust renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
  (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
  attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
  `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, and literal colors inline. The default `render(...)`
  injects the renderer's built-in `<style>` block (preflight reset + design
  tokens + `.pathland-*` component defaults) into every document — no
  `/tailwind.css`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` /
  `renderLinkedDebug(...)` instead emit a content-hashed
  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{cssBase}/{baseCssName()}">`; token overrides
  and fit-band rules stay inline. `baseCss()` / `baseCssName()` bind the Rust
  `pathland_html_base_css[_name]` exports so the Spring/Quarkus starters serve
  the renderer-owned bytes immutable. A missing linked export degrades to the
  inline document.
- **Icon glyphs from the shared renderer**: `iconSvg(String name)` binds the
  Rust `pathland_html_icon_svg` export over the C ABI — the full inline `<svg>`
  for a canonical `ICON_NAME` (unknown/extension names → the renderer's
  fallback glyph, never null). Hosts serve `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from
  it (Spring/Quarkus route a few lines in their starters), so the DOM client's
  lazy icon fetch gets the same glyph data SSR inlines from — one Rust source,
  no per-platform static icon files. `HtmlRendererTest` covers it.
- **Demos use the shim**: `SessionApp` no longer calls `applyFrame`; SSR renders
  the mount frame through `HtmlRenderer.render(sink.frame(), rootId)`. The
  renderer is compiled once at startup.
- **Text fields share one component class**: `TEXT_FIELD` inputs and `TEXT_EDITOR`
  textareas render with `class="pathland-input"` (Tailwind-style inset-outline
  styling from the Rust renderer's CSS); the copied `@pathland/dom-renderer`
  bundle (content-hashed `dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` in both demos) mirrors the
  class so delta-created fields hydrate identically.

## Removed (September 2026)

- `compileTailwind(overrideCss)` and the `pathland_tailwind_compile` binding are
  **deleted** — the renderer is inline-only now and needs no compiler. The demo
  `/tailwind.css` endpoints (`TailwindCssController` / `TailwindCssResource`)
  and the `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/tailwind.css">` in both `SessionApp`
  files are removed.

## Not implemented / gaps

- **Typography uses the platform system font stack** (`system-ui,
  -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, …`) — the Rust renderer's document head
  makes no external/webfont requests, so the demo pages render without loading
  any font files and work offline. An app can still override `font.body.family`
  via a `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` to any font it hosts.
- The shim is unaffected by the Rust renderer's September 2026 shell alignment
  (SPACER/MENU/STEPPER/GAUGE/PICKER markup now matches the DOM client's runtime
  shells); the demos' SSR output reflects the Rust renderer as-is, pinned by the
  `pathland-html-golden` conformance harness. `HtmlRendererTest` covers the
  semantic-role → element mapping (`NAVIGATION`→`<nav>`, `HEADER`→`<h2>`,
  `TEXT_STYLE` headings) and the DSL's rejection of non-semantic role codes,
  plus media rendering (a `VIDEO` surface bound to its `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` —
  native `<video controls>` + `data-pathland-controller`, the non-visual hidden
  controller shell, image `alt` from the accessibility label,
  `ContentMode Fill`→`cover`).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-render-html` — JNA shim tests (skip when the Rust dylib
is absent), including the linked stylesheet link + `baseCss`/`baseCssName`
exposure; part of the non-demo reactor run on JDK 17.

# pathland-render-html

The HTML renderer: a stateless, streaming pure function of the opcode stream
that maps declarative frames onto HTML elements — Pathland's server-side /
remote-projection target.

Part of [Pathland](https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland). Depends on
[`pathland-core`](https://crates.io/crates/pathland-core) and
[`pathland-core-transport`](https://crates.io/crates/pathland-core-transport).

Apache-2.0.

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# Multi-stage image for the Pathland Quarkus SSR demo (server-side HTML + /ws deltas).
# Build context is the repository root — the renderer and view-core jars embed
# their Rust cdylibs, and the demo module needs the Java reactor sources:
#
#   docker build -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile -t pathland-quarkus-demo .
#
# See docs/DEPLOY.md.

# --- Stage 1: the Rust HTML renderer + inline-Markdown cdylibs (embedded into jars) ---
FROM rust:1-slim AS rust
WORKDIR /src
COPY lib/rust ./lib/rust
RUN cargo build --manifest-path lib/rust/Cargo.toml \
    -p pathland-render-html -p pathland-markdown-capi

# --- Stage 2: the Java reactor + the Quarkus app (jars embed the dylibs) ---
FROM maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-17 AS java
WORKDIR /src
COPY --from=rust /src/lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so \
     lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so
COPY --from=rust /src/lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_markdown.so \
     lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_markdown.so
COPY lib/java ./lib/java
# Include the extension's deployment module in the reactor: the runtime module's
# quarkus-extension-maven-plugin validates its dependencies against it, and it is
# not a Maven dependency of the demo (so -am alone would omit it).
RUN mvn -q -B -f lib/java/pom.xml \
    -pl pathland-quarkus-demo,pathland-quarkus-deployment \
    -am package -Dmaven.test.skip=true

# --- Stage 3: runtime (JRE only) ---
FROM eclipse-temurin:17-jre
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=java /src/lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/target/quarkus-app/ /app/
EXPOSE 8080
ENV QUARKUS_HTTP_PORT=8080
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-Xms64m", "-Xmx256m", "-jar", "/app/quarkus-run.jar"]---

- name: Verify the protocol manifest is current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest
          git -C ../.. diff --exit-code -- spec/protocol.tsv

      # The shared engine traces are emitted by the canonical Rust engine and
      # compared byte-for-byte by the JVM engine test. Verify the committed
      # fixtures have not drifted from the current engine behavior.
      - name: Verify engine trace fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --check

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

      - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: ./check-wasm.sh

      # The Java HTML renderer shim needs the Rust renderer cdylib (the jar embeds
      # it so it travels with the artifact). Build it here and hand it to the java
      # job via an artifact.
      - name: Build the HTML renderer and markdown cdylibs
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-render-html -p pathland-markdown-capi

      - name: Upload the renderer dylib for the java job
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so
          retention-days: 1

      - name: Upload the markdown dylib for the java job
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-markdown-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_markdown.so
          retention-days: 1

  java:
    name: Java (Maven reactor, JDK ${{ matrix.java }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [rust]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java: ['17', '21', '25']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Whole-stack floor is Java 17 (maven.compiler.release=17; JNA native binding,
      # thread-local environment); the matrix proves every LTS from 17.
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
          cache: maven

      # The renderer jar embeds the Rust cdylib (built by the rust job). Restore it
      # into the debug dir the jar-embed step copies.

content.text:
## Findings

**Premise correction:** the protocol engine is *already* Kotlin on the JVM. `pathland-view-core` implements opcodes, the diff emitter, signals, the `PLPL` codec, and is byte-checked against Rust by `ProtocolManifestTest` + `EngineTraceTest`. The JVM server path only pulls in **two** Rust dylibs through JNA:

- `libpathland_render_html` (`pathland-render-html`, ~5.9k LOC) — the real question
- `libpathland_markdown` (`pathland-markdown`, ~520 LOC)

So this is not "Rust protocol vs Kotlin protocol"; it's "keep the SSR HTML renderer in Rust, or reimplement it in Kotlin." The renderer is a pure function of the frame and depends only on `pathland-core`/`pathland-core-transport`, so a port is mechanically feasible.

## Does GraalVM care? Yes — mainly packaging, not speed

Today nothing targets native-image: CI is JVM-only and the Quarkus `Dockerfile` ships a JRE + jars. If you add Quarkus/Spring native later:

- **JNA itself works** under `native-image` (JNA 5.14 ships metadata), but it is not zero-config: reachability/reflection for the `Library` interface plus resource registration for the embedded dylib.
- The jar-extraction path (`getResourceAsStream("/META-INF/native/...")` → temp dir) needs `quarkus.native.resources.includes=META-INF/native/**`, and breaks in hardened containers with read-only/noexec `/tmp`.
- Avoiding extraction means shipping the `.so`/`.dylib` beside the executable and setting `-Dpathland.render.html.lib=...` — which forfeits the "single binary" benefit native images are for.
- A **pure Kotlin renderer** AOT-compiles in: no JNA, no dlopen, no resource extraction, no sidecar lib, one executable. That is a genuine operational difference.
- Runtime performance is a wash (the Rust code is already native); only minor JNA startup/init differs.

## Tradeoffs of porting

- Output must stay **byte-identical**: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-html-golden` treats Rust SSR as canonical and the TS DOM client asserts the same fixtures. A Kotlin port needs a golden test against those fixtures before it can be trusted.
- It creates a second SSR implementation. The repo deliberately removed the Java renderer (`e9aade28`) for a "single renderer, every language" story. The Rust crate is still the cross-language/C-ABI projection target for non-JVM hosts.
- Feature velocity: every new component/property must land in both renderers (mitigated by the golden harness — the TS client already proves cross-renderer drift is testable).

## Recommendation

- **If GraalVM native is on the roadmap now:** port `pathland-render-html` to Kotlin in the JVM module, keep the Rust crate for non-JVM hosts, and wire `pathland-html-golden` into both (port `pathland-markdown` too — it's tiny). This gives you true single-binary native images.
- **If native is speculative:** don't port. Keep the one Rust renderer and add native-image config only when needed (resource include + `pathland.render.html.lib` sidecar). Porting now is a large change for no current deployment gain.
- The protocol should stay where it is (Kotlin on the JVM, Rust canonical for non-JVM); there is no benefit to moving that.

Which direction do you want to plan for?

content.text:
That goal clarifies the decision: **for a "Maven dependency, then run" experience, the JVM path should be pure JVM.** Today `pathland-view-core` is already pure Kotlin, but `pathland-render-html` and `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` load per-platform Rust dylibs via JNA, which is exactly what breaks "just add the dep": the jar only works on the four shipped OS/arch combos, fails on musl/Alpine and unshipped arches, extracts to `/tmp`, and needs extra config under GraalVM native-image.

## Recommended direction

Port the **HTML renderer** and the **Markdown parser** to the JVM, keep the Rust renderers for Rust/non-JVM hosts, and make the existing golden fixtures the contract between them. That gives:

- One Maven artifact set that runs on any JVM/OS/arch — no dylib matrix, no extraction, no `java.library.path`.
- GraalVM native-image works with no JNA/reachability/resource plumbing → true single executable.
- The Rust HTML renderer remains available for Swift/.NET/cross-language projection, guarded by the same fixtures.

## Plan

**1. Port Markdown (small, ~520 LOC) — unblocks pure `pathland-view-core`**
- Replace the JNA `Markdown.java` with a pure Kotlin parser matching `pathland-markdown` semantics (bold/italic/code/strike/links and edge cases).
- Keep the `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` API; `isAvailable()` becomes `true`.
- Add parity tests; remove the markdown dylib embed/staging from `pathland-view-core` and release/CI.

**2. Port the HTML renderer into `lib/java/pathland-render-html` (~6k LOC)**
- Reimplement decode → retained output tree → HTML over the existing `ProtocolFrame`/`FrameCodec` (no native boundary).
- Port the supporting tables: roles, tokens, icons, typography, media shell, toggle/date modes, attributed text, proxy view, fit bands, linked/inline CSS and debug comments.
- Embed `base.css` + `base.css.name` as classpath resources from the shared synced assets (or generate a constant at build time so native-image needs no resource config).
- Keep `HtmlRenderer`'s public API identical (Kotlin `@JvmStatic`), so `PathlandSession`, Spring and Quarkus need no changes.
- Remove JNA, the antrun native embed, and platform-resolution code.

**3. Enforce parity**
- Add a JVM golden test that renders the committed `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/*.{plpl,html}` and asserts byte equality (mirrors the TS conformance test).
- Keep `pathland-html-golden` as fixture producer; CI runs Rust check + TS conformance + JVM golden. Any HTML output change updates Rust, fixtures, and Kotlin in one change.
- Drop the Java job's native-artifact handoff, the release native staging for the jars, and the Rust stage in the Quarkus `Dockerfile`.

**4. Prove the payoff**
- Add a package/publish check: a fresh project declaring the starter dependency gets a working SSR page with no native setup.
- Add a Quarkus native CI job (`-Pnative`) verifying SSR + `/ws` + base CSS + icons in the native executable.
- Update `AGENTS.md` and all affected `status.md` files.

**Tradeoff to accept:** two HTML implementations (Rust for non-JVM, Kotlin for JVM). The golden fixtures already exist for exactly this (they currently guard Rust vs TS), so drift is testable — but every new component/property now lands in both renderers.

If that cost isn't worth it yet, the cheaper interim is to keep Rust and only add native-image config (resource include + sidecar dylib + `pathland.render.html.lib`) — but it does not deliver the universal "add a dep and run" you described.

content.text:
You're not giving up optimization by going pure Java.

**On Java vs Kotlin vs Rust for these pieces:**
- Java and Kotlin compile to the same JVM bytecode; HotSpot and GraalVM `native-image` treat them identically. No runtime cost.
- For `native-image`, pure Java is actually *less* surface than Kotlin (no `kotlin-stdlib` metadata/reflection in that code path) and vastly simpler than JNA (no reachability metadata, no dylib resource, no `/tmp` extraction).
- The current Markdown path costs *more* than a pure-Java parser: allocate JNA `Memory`, UTF-8 encode, cross the FFI, parse in Rust, copy the payload back, then `AttributedString.decode`. A pure-Java parser constructs the model directly and skips the encode/decode round-trip. It's likely **faster end-to-end**, not slower.
- Raw Rust parsing may win on huge inputs, but Markdown is parsed at emission time and `parseOrPlain` caches 512 results — irrelevant.
- One caveat: `AttributedString` is Kotlin. Pure-Java `Markdown` can still build it via its `@JvmStatic` factories, so the parser is pure Java while the model stays put. Fully Kotlin-free would require moving the model too — not worth it.

So the scope I'd take: **non-DSL infrastructure (parsers, renderer, codecs) in Java; the authoring DSL and engine stay Kotlin.** I'll treat the existing Kotlin protocol/engine as out of scope unless you say otherwise.

## Phase 1 — pure-Java Markdown

1. **Rewrite `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` as a direct port of `pathland-markdown/src/lib.rs`**
   - Escapes, `**`/`__` bold, `*`/`_` italic, `` ` `` code, `~~` strike, `[label](url)` with recursive label parsing, `***` outer/inner delimiter split, intraword underscore guards, unmatched markers literal, UTF-8 **byte** offsets.
   - Build `AttributedString` via `AttributedString.of(...)` + `StyleRun`/`TextAttribute` factories; return directly.
   - Keep the public API (`parse`, `parseOrPlain`, `containsMarkdownSyntax`); `isAvailable()` becomes `true`; delete all JNA/dylib-resolution code and keep the bounded cache.

2. **Tests**
   - Port every Rust parser test with exact assertions on text/runs/links/offsets; remove the `assumeTrue(isAvailable())` skips.
   - Add a DSL-level test asserting `Text("**hi**")` produces the expected `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` bytes (proves wire parity with the Rust format).
   - Recommended: a small shared fixture corpus (input → expected `{text,runs,links}`) consumed by both Rust and Java tests, so the two parsers can't drift.

3. **Build/CI cleanup (Markdown-only)**
   - `pathland-view-core/pom.xml`: remove the `embed-native-markdown` antrun execution; keep the JNA dependency (still used by `ffm/PathlandCore.kt` for the desktop ring).
   - `ci.yml`: drop the `pathland-markdown-native` upload/download steps.
   - `release.yml`: drop the `markdown-native` staging and the `pathland-markdown-capi` build from the Java path.
   - `Dockerfile`: remove `pathland-markdown-capi` from the Rust stage and its `.so` copy.
   - Root `pom.xml` / `scripts/lib.sh` `refresh-ide`: remove the `-p pathland-markdown-capi` build.
   - Keep the `pathland-markdown` + `-capi` Rust crates for the Rust DSL and non-JVM hosts.

4. **Docs + verification**
   - Update `lib/java/pathland-view-core/status.md` and `AGENTS.md` (JVM parser is pure Java; Rust parser is canonical for Rust/non-JVM).
   - Verify `mvn -q -B test -pl pathland-view-core` passes with **no** `java.library.path`, the jar contains no `META-INF/native/libpathland_markdown*`, and `Markdown.isAvailable()` is true.

Phase 2 then applies the same pattern to `pathland-render-html` in Java, guarded by the existing `pathland-html-golden` fixtures.

One scope check before I start: for "non-UI-DSL elements", do you want **only new/ported infrastructure in Java** (Markdown, HTML renderer), or do you also want the **existing Kotlin protocol/engine emitter migrated to Java**? The latter is a much larger, riskier refactor with no runtime benefit, and I'd recommend leaving it in Kotlin.
Only new and create an issue for existing engine/protocol

## Final plan

**Scope decisions**
- New/ported non-DSL infrastructure → **Java** (`Markdown`, HTML renderer).
- Existing Kotlin engine/protocol → **left as-is**; tracked by a new GitHub issue instead of migrated now.
- Rust renderers stay for Rust/non-JVM hosts; the `pathland-html-golden` fixtures remain the output contract.
- Keep Kotlin for the authoring DSL and the engine it drives.

---

### Phase 1 — Markdown → pure Java (no native)

**Code**
- Rewrite `lib/java/pathland-view-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/markdown/Markdown.java` as a direct port of `lib/rust/crates/pathland-markdown/src/lib.rs`:
  - escapes, `**`/`__` bold, `*`/`_` italic, `` ` `` code, `~~` strike, `[label](url)` (recursive labels), `***` outer/inner split, intraword underscore guards, unmatched markers literal, UTF-8 **byte** offsets.
  - Build `AttributedString` via `AttributedString.of(...)` + `StyleRun`/`TextAttribute` factories; return directly (no encode/decode round trip).
  - Keep `parse`, `parseOrPlain`, `containsMarkdownSyntax`; `isAvailable()` → `true`; keep the bounded cache.
  - Delete all JNA/`Native.load`/dylib-resolution code.

**Tests**
- Port every Rust parser test into `MarkdownTest` with exact `text`/`runs`/`links`/offset assertions; remove `assumeTrue(isAvailable())`.
- Add a DSL-level test asserting `Text("**hi**")` emits the expected `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` bytes.
- Add a shared fixture corpus (input → expected model) consumed by both Rust and Java tests to prevent drift.

**Build/CI**
- `pathland-view-core/pom.xml`: remove the `embed-native-markdown` antrun execution and the `java.library.path` test arg (keep the JNA dependency — still used by `ffm/PathlandCore.kt` for the desktop ring).
- `ci.yml`: drop the `pathland-markdown-native` upload/download.
- `release.yml`: drop markdown staging + `pathland-markdown-capi` from the Java path.
- `Dockerfile`: remove `pathland-markdown-capi` and its `.so` copy.
- Root `pom.xml` / `scripts/lib.sh` `refresh-ide`: drop `-p pathland-markdown-capi`.
- Keep the `pathland-markdown` / `-capi` crates for Rust and non-JVM hosts.

**Docs**
- Update `lib/java/pathland-view-core/status.md` and the `AGENTS.md` line describing the JVM parser.

---

### Phase 2 — HTML renderer → pure Java

- Reimplement `dev.pathland.render.html.HtmlRenderer` in Java over the existing `ProtocolFrame`/`FrameCodec`, mirroring `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html` (~6k LOC: decode → output tree → HTML).
- Port supporting tables: `role_spec`, `token_spec`, `icons`, typography, media shell, toggle/date modes, attributed text, proxy view, fit bands, inline/linked CSS, debug comments.
- Embed `base.css` + `base.css.name` as resources (copy the synced assets via `maven-resources-plugin`; revisit a neutral canonical location later).
- Keep the `HtmlRenderer` public API identical (`@JvmStatic`) so `PathlandSession`, Spring, and Quarkus need no changes; `isAvailable()`/`tryInstance()` become always-available.
- Remove JNA + the antrun native embed from `pathland-render-html/pom.xml`; drop the renderer native staging from CI/release and the Rust stage in the Dockerfile.
- Acceptance: a JVM golden test renders `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/*.{plpl,html}` byte-for-byte (mirrors the TS conformance test).
- Optional: extend `pathland-ts-codegen` to emit the role/token tables for Java too.

---

### Phase 3 — GitHub issue for the existing engine/protocol

First step after plan approval (I can't create it in plan mode):

- **Title:** `Evaluate migrating the Kotlin protocol + engine to Java`
- **Body:** context (non-DSL infra moving to Java for Maven-dep-and-run + native-image); current state (`pathland-view-core` engine/protocol/emitter is Kotlin but already pure-JVM, so it doesn't block either goal); decision asked (is “pure Java for non-DSL” a hard rule for existing code?); constraints (wire output pinned by `ProtocolManifestTest`, `EngineTraceTest`, `pathland-engine-golden`; no expected performance gain); proposed approach (module-by-module migration with golden guards, Kotlin DSL retained); non-goals (no wire/behavior changes). No labels assumed.

---

### Verification
- `mvn -q -B test -pl pathland-view-core` (no `java.library.path`), then the full reactor.
- Assert the built jars contain no `META-INF/native/libpathland_{markdown,render_html}*`.
- Run the Rust golden `--check`, TS conformance, and the new JVM golden tests.
- After Phase 2: build `pathland-quarkus-demo` with native-image as the proof of the end goal.

### Risks
- Exact HTML parity is the hard part (attribute order, whitespace, escaping, debug comments); the golden fixtures make drift testable.
- Dual maintenance of Rust + Java renderers — accepted, since fixtures already guard Rust vs TS.
- Keep `AttributedString`/`ProtocolFrame` in Kotlin for now; moving those is part of the Phase 3 issue if you later want the artifacts Kotlin-free.

input.content:
## Context

We are standardising non-UI-DSL infrastructure on **pure Java** so a developer can add a Maven dependency and run it on any JVM/OS/arch (and under GraalVM native-image) without shipping native libraries.

Current split:

- `pathland-view-core` protocol/engine/emitter/signals/router/state is **Kotlin** (already pure JVM — no native dependency, so it does not block "add a dependency and run" or native-image).
- The HTML renderer is a Rust cdylib over JNA (being ported to Java next).
- The inline Markdown parser was just ported to pure Java (Rust crate remains for Rust/non-JVM hosts).

The remaining question is whether the existing Kotlin engine/protocol should also be migrated to Java for language consistency.

## Decision to make

Is "pure Java for non-DSL code" a **hard rule** that applies to existing code, or a preference for new/ported code? If hard, this issue tracks the migration of the existing Kotlin protocol/engine.

## Constraints

- Wire output is pinned and must stay byte-identical:
  - `spec/protocol.tsv` + `ProtocolManifestTest`
  - `spec/engine-traces/` + `EngineTraceTest`
  - `pathland-engine-golden`
- No behaviour or wire changes.
- No expected runtime performance change: Kotlin and Java compile to the same JVM bytecode; GraalVM `native-image` treats both the same.
- The Kotlin authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`) stays Kotlin.

## Proposed approach (if pursued)

- Migrate module-by-module, starting with leaf value/codec types (opcode, constants, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`, `AttributedString`) and then the emitter/signals/router.
- Keep the golden suites as the guardrail for every step.
- Do not change packages or public APIs that hosts depend on unless necessary.

## Non-goals

- No protocol or wire changes.
- No DSL rewrite (Kotlin remains the authoring surface).
- No change to the Rust renderers/DSL.

## Acceptance

- A documented language policy (hard rule vs preference).
- If migrating: each step lands with `cargo test` + full `mvn test` green and the manifest/engine-trace golden checks unchanged.

## Release

1. Create a **GitHub Release** on `main` tagged `vX.Y.Z` (publish it).
2. The workflow runs:
   - `version` — derive + validate `X.Y.Z` from the tag.
   - `rust` — set the version, test the publishable crates, publish them to
     crates.io in dependency order, upload the `.crate` files.
   - `java-natives` — build `libpathland_render_html` and
     `libpathland_markdown` for windows-x86_64, linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64,
     macos-aarch64.
    - `java` — set the version, stage the natives into the renderer jar, run
      `mvn -P release deploy` to Maven Central (auto-published after validation).
    - `bump` — commit the version back to `main`.
    - `release-assets` — attach the `.crate` files, the Java main jars, and the
      native libs to the GitHub Release.

The Java deploy runs on **Maven 3.9.9** (pinned in the workflow): Maven 3.10

package dev.pathland.view.core.protocol

/**
 * A fixed-size 16-byte Pathland opcode (little-endian):
 *
 * `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32][B u32][C u32]`
 *
 * The component-named methods preserve the Java record accessor API
 * (`op.category()`, `op.b()`, …) used by the renderers, hosts, and tests.
 */
data class Opcode(
    val category: Int,
    val command: Int,
    val flags: Int,
    val a: Int,
    val b: Int,
    val c: Int,
) {
    fun category(): Int = category
    fun command(): Int = command
    fun flags(): Int = flags
    fun a(): Int = a
    fun b(): Int = b
    fun c(): Int = c

    /** Serialize to the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
    fun toBytes(): ByteArray {
        val out = ByteArray(SIZE)
        out[0] = category.toByte()
        out[1] = command.toByte()
        out[2] = flags.toByte()
        out[3] = (flags ushr 8).toByte()
        writeIntLE(out, 4, a)
        writeIntLE(out, 8, b)
        writeIntLE(out, 12, c)
        return out
    }

    companion object {
        const val SIZE = 16

        /** Deserialize from the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
        fun fromBytes(bytes: ByteArray): Opcode {
            require(bytes.size == SIZE) { "opcode must be $SIZE bytes" }
            return Opcode(
                bytes[0].toInt() and 0xFF,
                bytes[1].toInt() and 0xFF,
                (bytes[2].toInt() and 0xFF) or ((bytes[3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8),
                readIntLE(bytes, 4),
                readIntLE(bytes, 8),
                readIntLE(bytes, 12),
            )
        }

        private fun writeIntLE(out: ByteArray, offset: Int, value: Int) {
            out[offset] = value.toByte()
            out[offset + 1] = (value ushr 8).toByte()
            out[offset + 2] = (value ushr 16).toByte()
            out[offset + 3] = (value ushr 24).toByte()
        }

        private fun readIntLE(bytes: ByteArray, offset: Int): Int =
            (bytes[offset].toInt() and 0xFF) or
                ((bytes[offset + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
                ((bytes[offset + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
                ((bytes[offset + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
    }
}

        Boot, Quarkus, or any Java server.

            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>

                        <id>test-compile</id>

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# Multi-stage image for the Pathland Quarkus SSR demo (server-side HTML + /ws deltas).
# Build context is the repository root. The Java path is pure JVM (the HTML
# renderer is a Java port), so the image needs no Rust toolchain and the jar
# embeds no native library:
#
#   docker build -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile -t pathland-quarkus-demo .

# --- Stage 1: the Java reactor + the Quarkus app ---
FROM maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-17 AS java
WORKDIR /src
# The render-html module copies the generated base design from the Rust crate's
# committed assets; no Rust build is needed.
COPY lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets ./lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets
COPY lib/java ./lib/java
# Include the extension's deployment module in the reactor: the runtime module's
# quarkus-extension-maven-plugin validates its dependencies against it, and it is
# not a Maven dependency of the demo (so -am alone would omit it).
RUN mvn -q -B -f lib/java/pom.xml \
    -pl pathland-quarkus-demo,pathland-quarkus-deployment \
    -am package -Dmaven.test.skip=true

# --- Stage 2: runtime (JRE only) ---
FROM eclipse-temurin:17-jre
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=java /src/lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/target/quarkus-app/ /app/
EXPOSE 8080
ENV QUARKUS_HTTP_PORT=8080
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-Xms64m", "-Xmx256m", "-jar", "/app/quarkus-run.jar"]

# pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 6, 2026

The **pure-Java HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a behavioural
port of the Rust `pathland-render-html` crate. Stateless: each call decodes a
self-contained snapshot frame into a transient tree and renders it to HTML in
one pass. No JNA and no cdylib, so a Maven dependency runs on every platform and
under GraalVM native-image. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Pure-Java renderer**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` / `tryInstance()` /
  `isAvailable()` (always true); `render(frame, root)` /
  `renderFragment(frame, root)` / `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a
  self-contained snapshot in one pass. The public API is unchanged from the
  former JNA shim, so `PathlandSession`, Spring, and Quarkus need no changes.
- **Byte-identical Rust output**: `GoldenConformanceTest` renders every
  committed `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/*.plpl` fixture and compares the
  fragment to its `.html` fixture byte-for-byte (the same contract the TS DOM
  client asserts), including the delta base/change/result scenario.
- **Full renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
  (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
  attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
  `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, literal colors inline, attributed text, media
  surfaces/controllers, proxy views, grid rows/tracks, fit bands, and
  size-that-fits snapshots.
- **Built-in base design**: the generated `design/build/base.css` (synced into
  the Rust assets) is copied into the jar at build time and inlined by the
  default `render(...)`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` /
  `renderLinkedDebug(...)` emit a content-hashed
  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{cssBase}/{baseCssName()}">`; `baseCss()` /
  `baseCssName()` expose the renderer-owned bytes for immutable serving.
- **Debug comments**: `renderDebug` / `renderFragmentDebug` prefix every node
  with an HTML comment naming its component and decoded modifiers.
- **Icon glyphs**: `iconSvg(name)` returns the full inline `<svg>` for a
  canonical `ICON_NAME` (unknown names → the fallback glyph; `null` → `null`),
  so hosts serve `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from the same table SSR inlines.
- **Demos use the renderer**: the Spring Boot and Quarkus starters SSR through
  `HtmlRenderer`, and the DOM client hydrates in place.

## Not implemented / gaps

- **Typography uses the platform system font stack**; the document head makes no
  external/webfont requests.
- The renderer is a port of the Rust implementation, not a second source of
  truth: when the HTML output changes, update the Rust crate + golden fixtures
  and this port together (`GoldenConformanceTest` fails on drift).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-render-html` — the golden conformance suite plus the
DSL → emitter → frame → renderer round-trip tests. Part of the non-demo reactor
run on JDK 17/21/25 and under GraalVM native-image.

# pathland-render-html (Rust) — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 28, 2026

The **server-side / remote-projection HTML renderer**: a **stateless, streaming**
pure function of the opcode stream producing declarative HTML. Each render call
decodes a self-contained snapshot batch into a **transient** map, walks it once,
and emits HTML text out — no retained tree, zero cross-call state (Renderer
Statelessness). Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

## Design decision (decision A, September 2026): inline-all + built-in design system

Tailwind is **removed**. The renderer emits **everything inline** as CSS in a
single `style` attribute — no external compiler, no class system, no safelist:

- **All opcode properties render inline** (`style_css()` + `border_style()`),
  including the previously class-based enum surface (alignment, text alignment,
  text case, visible, font style/design, underline/strikethrough, clips-to-bounds,
  hit-testing, invert, truncation). **1 dp = 1 CSS px**.

  `render_document` (see "Built-in HTML base design" above), containing:
  - a **preflight reset** (vendored from Tailwind CSS, MIT — see

# Releasing Pathland

Publishing a **GitHub Release** (tagged `vX.Y.Z`) runs
`.github/workflows/release.yml`, which sets the version from the tag, builds and
publishes every artifact, attaches the built files to the Release, and commits
the version back to `main`:

| Ecosystem | Artifacts | Registry |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| Rust | `pathland-core`, `pathland-markdown`, `pathland-engine`, `pathland-view`, `pathland-core-transport`, `pathland-render-html` | crates.io |
| Java | `dev.pathland:*` libraries (incl. the renderer + view-core native libs for windows-x86_64, linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64) | Maven Central |

## Versioning (tag-driven)

**The tag drives the version** — no pre-bump commit is needed:

- The workflow writes `X.Y.Z` (from the tag `vX.Y.Z`) into
  `lib/rust/Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package] version` + the intra-workspace
  path-dep pins, via `cargo set-version --workspace`) and
  `lib/java/pom.xml` (via `mvn versions:set`) **in CI**, then publishes.
---
## Release

1. Create a **GitHub Release** on `main` tagged `vX.Y.Z` (publish it).
2. The workflow runs:
   - `version` — derive + validate `X.Y.Z` from the tag.
   - `rust` — set the version, test the publishable crates, publish them to
     crates.io in dependency order, upload the `.crate` files.
   - `java-natives` — build `libpathland_render_html` for windows-x86_64,
     linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64. (The JVM Markdown parser is
     pure Java, so no markdown native is staged for the jars.)
    - `java` — set the version, stage the natives into the renderer jar, run
      `mvn -P release deploy` to Maven Central (auto-published after validation).
    - `bump` — commit the version back to `main`.
    - `release-assets` — attach the `.crate` files, the Java main jars, and the
      native libs to the GitHub Release.

The Java deploy runs on **Maven 3.9.9** (pinned in the workflow): Maven 3.10
writes a `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
which the Portal rejects ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). The demos

# Deploying the Quarkus SSR demo

Runs the [Pathland Quarkus demo](pathland-quarkus-demo/) (server-side HTML at any
path + live `/ws` deltas) as a container — the application evidence for the Restack
proposal (issue #71, `docs/PREAPPLICATION-TODO.md`).

The image is multi-stage: it builds the Rust HTML renderer and inline-Markdown
cdylibs, embeds them into the Java `pathland-render-html` and `pathland-view-core`
jars, packages the Quarkus app, and runs it on a JRE 17 runtime.

## Build

From the repository root (build context must be the root — the embed step needs
the Rust dylib and the Java reactor sources):

```bash
docker build -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile -t pathland-quarkus-demo .
```

The Rust stage builds `libpathland_render_html.so`; the Java stage copies it into
`lib/rust/target/debug` so the renderer jar-embed step finds it. The JVM inline
Markdown parser is pure Java and needs no native build.

The image's Maven step selects both `pathland-quarkus-demo` and
`pathland-quarkus-deployment`. The deployment module is not a Maven dependency of
the demo, but the runtime extension descriptor validates its dependencies against
it; omitting it makes a fresh (empty `~/.m2`) build fail Quarkus extension
verification.

## Run locally

content.text:
Committed and Phase 2 is done.

**Commits on `feat/pure-java-markdown`**
- `6669c480` `refactor(jvm): pure-Java inline Markdown parser`
- `e854d83b` `refactor(jvm): pure-Java HTML renderer`

**Phase 2 result**
